obligation: G017 - decompose the per-token fixed cost
method: Ablate one stage at a time at seq=1 over 40 real decode steps with a live KV cache, patching __call__ at the TYPE. Every arm is verified to CHANGE THE LOGITS; a first attempt patched the INSTANCE, which Python ignores for dunder lookup, and produced a 100% unattributed residual that would have read as 'all overhead' if the control had not caught it.
ANSWER_why_quantized_decode_sits_at_18_2: Because only 17.4% of a quantized decode step is expert matmuls -- the ONLY stage byte reduction touches. Router+gather+combine is 28.2% and attention is 40.8%, and neither moves with expert bytes: 3.100 -> 2.488 ms (-20%) and 3.857 -> 3.600 ms (-6.7%) going from bf16 to q3, against expert matmuls 4.171 -> 1.530 ms (-63%). Quantization did exactly what it should to the part it governs; that part is a minority of the step.

CEILINGS_this_reorders_the_whole_optimis.reading: Making the expert organ COMPLETELY FREE -- the limit of all Gravity work on this specimen -- buys at most 1.21x decode. Attention is the largest single lever at 1.69x and the router/gather/combine path is 1.39x. The campaign has spent its entire effort on the smallest of the three.

CAVEATS: seq=8 prefill then 40 decode steps, so the KV cache is short and attention's share is dominated by fixed per-call cost rather than cache traffic; at long context attention would grow further, strengthening the conclusion.

Ablation replaces a stage with a zero tensor of the right shape, so it removes the stage's compute AND its output; downstream work on that output is also removed. The shares are therefore upper bounds on each stage, and they sum to more than 100% for that reason.
Dispatch COUNT is still unmeasured; this attributes wall time to stages, not to kernel launches.
